🧠 Reference: cddml-TemporalPatternMiner

File Name: temporal_pattern_miner.py

🔍 Description

An advanced project utilizing pandas, scikit-learn, statsmodels, and matplotlib to perform sophisticated time series analysis, including anomaly detection, forecasting, and pattern recognition on the Air Quality dataset.

💻 Python Code

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
from statsmodels.tsa.seasonal import STL
from statsmodels.tsa.arima.model import ARIMA
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error
from math import sqrt

# Load dataset
url: str = 'https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/00360/AirQualityUCI.csv'
df: pd.DataFrame = pd.read_csv(url, sep=';', decimal=',', parse_dates=[['Date', 'Time']], na_values=-200)

# Preprocess
df.dropna(axis=1, how='all', inplace=True)
df.dropna(inplace=True)
df.rename(columns={'Date_Time': 'datetime'}, inplace=True)
df.set_index('datetime', inplace=True)
df = df.resample('H').mean()

# Select target variable
target_col: str = 'CO(GT)'
series: pd.Series = df[target_col]

# Anomaly detection
model_if: IsolationForest = IsolationForest(contamination=0.01, random_state=42)
df['anomaly'] = model_if.fit_predict(series.values.reshape(-1, 1))

# STL decomposition
stl = STL(series, seasonal=13)
res = stl.fit()
res.plot()
plt.show()

# ARIMA forecasting
train_size: int = int(len(series) * 0.8)
train, test = series[:train_size], series[train_size:]

model_arima = ARIMA(train, order=(5,1,0))
model_fit = model_arima.fit()
forecast = model_fit.forecast(steps=len(test))
rmse: float = sqrt(mean_squared_error(test, forecast))
print(f'RMSE: {rmse:.3f}')

# Plot forecast
plt.figure(figsize=(10,5))
plt.plot(train.index, train, label='Train')
plt.plot(test.index, test, label='Test')
plt.plot(test.index, forecast, label='Forecast')
plt.legend()
plt.show()
